Research
NEW ONLINE
Marine bacteria cooperate to break down complex algal carbohydrates
Marine algae produce sulfated carbohydrates called fucoidans that are chemically too complex for any bacteria to digest alone. Instead, marine bacteria split the task between them in a modular fashion: some strains degrade the molecular backbone, whereas others remove the side branches.
Antimatter: coming soon to a lab near you?
Antiprotons have been transported by road at CERN. This advance might one day enable laboratories outside the site to use antimatter in their experiments.
Nancy Paul, Davide Gamba
Molecular computation that rolls energetically downhill
A DNA-based computer that operates by relaxing to thermodynamic equilibrium has been demonstrated on ten molecular programs, which completed computations in as little as one minute. Some programs were rerun using distinct inputs up to 25 times and others were scaled up to 100-bit computations — although this slowed them down substantially.
Development of a random background to understand ligand optimization
An approach to improve efficiency and establish a background expectation for ligand potency optimization is described.
Xinyu Xu, Olivier Mailhot, Galen J. Correy et al.
Turning scientific research papers into interactive AI agents
Scientific knowledge is mostly stored in static papers. An automated framework called Paper2Agent can now transform each paper into an active artificial intelligence agent — a virtual corresponding author that answers questions, applies the paper’s methods to new data, and collaborates with other paper agents. This makes research easier to reproduce, reuse and extend.
Developmental xenocortication using human-derived organoids in mice
Xenocortication with human neurons enables circuit- and behaviour-level analysis of neurodevelopment in mice.
Konstantin Kaganovsky, Kevin W. Kelley, Tilo Gschwind et al.
Mitochondrial fission factor senses and governs ferroptosis
The mitochondrial–peroxisomal fission adaptor MFF is identified as a selective pro-ferroptotic mediator, and the newly developed MFF–SPARK sensor enables high-content screening of ferroptosis-sensitizing compounds and the discovery of upstream regulators of MFF.
Songjun Dai, Xiaoyan Dai, Tingting Zhang et al.
Reimagining research papers as interactive and reliable AI agents
Paper2Agent converts research papers into interactive artificial intelligence (AI) agents by turning manuscripts, code and data into model context protocol-based tool-invoking systems that reproduce original results, answer new scientific queries and collaborate to generate novel insights.
Jiacheng Miao, Joe R. Davis, Yaohui Zhang et al.
Electroluminescent photoresists extending lithographic scaling to OLEDs
Electroluminescent photoresists synthesized via atom transfer radical polymerization can be directly patterned by ultraviolet and electron-beam lithography, and used to fabricate monolithic, multicolour organic-light-emitting-diode (OLED) micro-pixel arrays.
Shao-Wei Lo, Sunil B. Shivarudraiah, Zhan-Hong Lin et al.
Mutational constraints on RSV F and its neutralization by antibodies
How respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) mutations affect antibody neutralization is defined, and a biophysical model of the mechanism is provided, to show how Fab potency and epitope specificity combine to determine the effects of viral mutations on antibody neutralization.
Cassandra A. L. Simonich, Teagan E. McMahon, Gavin Juviler et al.
Evolution and heterogeneity of lethal metastatic bladder cancer subtypes
A rapid autopsy programme provides valuable resources to enable detailed molecular and genetic analyses of the temporal evolution of aggressive histological subtypes and therapy resistance in metastatic bladder cancer.
Pushpa Itagi, Samantha L. Schuster, Sonali Arora et al.
Nearly one in seven young, male white voters in the US support white nationalism
Three national surveys reveal how factors such as gender, age, political alignment and income are correlated with support for white nationalism in the United States.
Jennifer Chudy
Topographic structure and function of locus coeruleus noradrenaline neurons
Dorsal and ventral noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus form topographic subpopulations whose projection patterns and activity encode choice switching, reward-prediction errors and disregard of reward-predictive cues, supporting flexible learning behaviour.
Zhixiao Su, Polina Kosillo, Kanghoon Jung et al.
A retinoic acid autoregulatory loop governing prefrontal–motor arealization
MEIS2, encoding a transcription factor linked to intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, is a key hub of a retinoic-acid-associated gene regulatory network.
Lin Yang, Mikihito Shibata, Saejeong Park et al.
Road transport of trapped antiprotons
Researchers demonstrate successful road transport of trapped antiprotons, establishing a practical method for moving antimatter to quieter laboratories and substantially improving future tests of matter–antimatter symmetry.
M. Leonhardt, J. Morgner, F. Abbass et al.
Transcriptional activation of plant immunity by salicylic acid
A mechanistic basis for how the hormone salicylic acid promotes transcriptional activation during plant immune responses is described.
Songwen Zhang, Madeline Gish, Huan Li et al.
Rapid patient-specific neural networks for X-ray to volume registration
xvr makes pan-anatomical 2D/3D rigid registration accessible to broad clinical and research communities.
Vivek Gopalakrishnan, David-Dimitris Chlorogiannis, Andrew Abumoussa et al.
Mechanisms of Transcriptional Regulation by Salicylic Acid Receptors
Yujun Peng, Hainan Tian, Zhenhua Ming et al.
Targeted genomic integration and rearrangement using prime assembly
Prime assembly enables RNA-guided integration of medium-to-large DNA sequences in human cells without requiring double-strand breaks or cell cycle progression, and supports exon recoding, transgene insertion and megabase-scale rearrangements.
Sébastien Levesque, Nozomu Kawashima, Gue-Ho Hwang et al.
Sex without crossovers mimics clonal reproduction in Rhynchospora tenuis
Rhynchospora tenuis undergoes obligate, genome-wide achiasmy in both male and female meiosis.
Meng Zhang, Marco Castellani, Stefan Steckenborn et al.
Scalable near-real-time Bayesian phylogenetics for outbreaks with Delphy
Delphy makes near-real-time and scalable Bayesian phylogenetics possible for growing viral outbreaks, enabling public health bodies anywhere to analyse and react to their own data with state-of-the-art accuracy and minimal friction.
Patrick Varilly, Mark Schifferli, Katherine Yang et al.
Tumour cells shape their environment to protect them from the immune system
A subset of pancreatic cancer cells express the genes SERPINE1 or SERPINB2, which form a molecular mesh around them. This sticky matrix helps to retain immunosuppressive cells and exclude the immune cells that kill cancer cells. Disrupting this process in mice improves immune control of pancreatic tumours and sensitizes them to immunotherapy.
Cohesin reshapes replication fork contacts to aid fork slowing and reversal
Cohesin-mediated loop extrusion limits sister-fork coupling and tethers nearby replication forks under replication stress, promoting fork reversal and slowing fork progression to safeguard genome stability.
Daniel González-Acosta, Daniel Giménez-Llorente, Melani Rodrigues et al.
Identification of broadly tumour-reactive γδ TCRs from multiple myeloma
A machine-learning algorithm, PreGame, is developed to identify tumour-reactive γδ T cells from single-cell CITE sequencing data, and expansion of this cell population can be used as a biomarker of therapeutic response.
Michael St. Paul, Liam D. Hendrikse, Fan Ying et al.
Predictors and prevalence of support for white nationalism in the United States
Explicit support for white nationalism is uncommon overall, but higher among young white men, disadvantaged and politically disaffected white people, conservatives, Republicans, and those with primarily online friendships.
Patrick J. Egan, James Bisbee, Joshua A. Tucker
Quality control of glycogen through direct ubiquitylation by RNF213
Matthew C. J. Yip, Katerina Naydenova, Elsje G. Otten et al.
Encoded and non-genetic protein variants expand human functional proteome
Vyacheslav Tretyachenko, Tehila Leiman, David Morgenstern et al.

Articles

Overmassive black holes and little red dots naturally form in simulations
Observations from the JWST reveal an unexpectedly abundant population of little red dots and overmassive black holes in the early Universe, which are confirmed by their formation in fully cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulations.
Sunmyon Chon, Shingo Hirano, Tomoaki Ishiyama et al.
Continuous-wave laser absorption spectroscopy of the thorium-229 nucleus
Absorption spectroscopy of thorium-229 nuclear excited states in a thorium-doped calcium fluoride crystal demonstrates a path towards a much more efficient way to build a highly stable and robust solid-state optical nuclear clock.
I. Morawetz, T. Riebner, L. Toscani De Col et al.
Electrically controllable superconducting memory effect in UTe2
 Observations of a memory effect in the p-wave superconductor candidate UTe2, which can be controlled by varying the strength and duration of the electrically applied stimuli, are described.
Zheyu Wu, Hanyi Chen, Mengmeng Long et al.
Heterogeneous photonic integration of single-crystalline nanomembranes
A framework consisting of advanced epitaxy and layer lift-off techniques uses heterogeneous photonic integration of single-crystalline nanomembranes to infuse desired functionalities into silicon and silicon nitride photonics, demonstrating ultraefficient electro-optical and magneto-optical modulation.
Yuan Meng, Wenbo Mao, Zhihao Xu et al.
A thermodynamically favoured molecular computer
Scaffolded DNA Computer performs diverse computations while thermodynamically relaxing towards equilibrium, demonstrating simplicity, reusability, speed, robustness and scalability of the approach by running 10 programs, including parity, multiplication and 25-bit addition.
Tristan Stérin, Abeer Eshra, Constantine Glen Evans et al.
Molecular-level observation of the self-assembly of a virus-like particle
Using mass photometry combined with a single-molecule trapping method allows real-time monitoring of the assembly of individual virus-like particles with molecular resolution, enabling observation and quantification of their self-assembly pathways and dynamics.
Roi Asor, Dan Loewenthal, Diana Melnyk et al.
Probing far-from-equilibrium dynamics of electrical double layers
A new framework combining experimental and computational methods to track ions and water present at an electrode interface allows the molecular structure and evolution of electrical double layers far from equilibrium to be discovered.
Xiao-Yu Li, Yu-Chen Cai, Zhao-Dong Meng et al.
Anodic Pd membrane H2 extraction enhances thermochemical dehydrogenation
An electrochemical cell with molten hydroxide and a Pd membrane actively extracts H2 and thereby boosts ammonia and methylcyclohexane conversion, while also delivering purified H2 ready for use.
Rui Zeng, Julian Ufert, Bryan Y. Tang et al.
Atmospheric CH4 plateau sustained by NOx emission rise and southward shift
The atmospheric methane (CH4) plateau can be explained by tropical hydroxyl radical enhancement primarily driven by a global rise and spatial redistribution of nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions towards developing regions and the oceans.
Yu Zhu, Lu Shen, Gang Liu et al.
Operational tropical cyclone forecasting with AI
An AI forecasting system called WeatherNext Cyclones can predict the track, intensity (maximum wind speed) and size of tropical cyclones with an accuracy gain over leading operational models comparable to a decade of progress in numerical forecasting.
Ferran Alet, Tom R. Andersson, Ilan Price et al.
Mobile education builds resilience during shocks in five countries
Remote phone-based targeted tutoring in five countries produced large, cost-effective learning gains during school closures, outperforming text messaging and working effectively when delivered by governments or non-governmental organizations to strengthen education resilience.
Noam Angrist, Micheal Ainomugisha, Sai Pramod Bathena et al.
Pines grow faster and are more drought resilient in the Southern Hemisphere
Non-native conifers from the Northern Hemisphere grow faster and are more drought resistant and resilient in the Southern Hemisphere, where they seem to escape the growth–stress-tolerance trade-off.
Alex Fajardo, Antonio Gazol, J. Julio Camarero et al.
FNIP1 variants are associated with favourable metabolism in 1 million humans
The FNIP1 pathway has a role in human energy metabolism, and its inhibition is a potential therapeutic strategy in cardiometabolic disease.

Human brain organoids record the passage of time over multiple years
Human brain organoids were developed for over five years in culture to demonstrate that brain cells can continue to mature and record the passage of time, following human-specific endogenous programs, even outside the context of the organism.
Irene Faravelli, Noelia Antón-Bolaños, Anqi Wei et al.
Stimulation modulates gene-linked cell assemblies in the human brain
Stimulation of human cortex reorganizes neural assemblies and induces cell-type-specific gene regulatory programs, establishing an ex vivo framework that links stimulation parameters to circuit and transcriptional responses for designing targeted neuromodulatory therapies.
Haley Moore, Mantre Dehnad, Anne Freelin et al.
Diverse bacterial pattern recognition receptors sense the core phage proteome
Systematic analysis of prokaryotic STAND NTPases—relatives of animal and plant immune receptors—uncovers diverse antiviral sensors that detect most of the core structural and replicative proteins of bacteriophages.
Hyunbin Lee, Sofia Luengo-Woods, Jianxiu Zhang et al.
The Virtual Tissues foundation model resolves spatial proteomics across scales
Virtual Tissues (VirTues), a foundation model for spatial proteomics that captures tissue organization across scales, supports marker reconstruction, cell segmentation and typing, niche annotation, spatial biomarker discovery and patient stratification across heterogeneous panels and datasets.
Johann Wenckstern, Eeshaan Jain, Benedikt von Querfurth et al.
Antigen presentation by CD40+MHC-II+ astrocytes promotes CNS autoimmunity
Astrocytes promote central nervous system (CNS) immunity through antigen presentation and activation of CD40 in astrocytes by CD40L expressed by CD4+ T cells in a model of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.

A tumour-derived organoid biobank maps cancer gene dependencies
A clinically annotated multi-omic organoid resource with matched tumour samples from 256 patients across 5 cancers maps gene dependencies, reveals subtype-specific vulnerabilities and uncovers treatment-driven changes, expanding mechanistic insight and models for precision oncology.
C. Herranz-Ors, S. G. Bhosle, A. E. Beck et al.
A compendium of next-generation patient-derived models for diverse cancers
The international collaboration of the Human Cancer Models Initiative presents a comprehensive resource of next-generation cancer models from 2,780 donors with 25 cancer types and integrated tumour–model genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic analyses.
Dina ElHarouni, Mushriq Al-Jazrawe, Seongmin Choi et al.
A dependency map enhanced with next-generation 3D cancer models
Integration of genome-scale CRISPR screening data from traditional cell lines and next-generation cancer models expands the representation of tumour subtypes and genomic alterations in The Cancer Dependency Map.
James V. Neiswender, Samuel Maffa, Lisa Brenan et al.
Aneuploidy selects for the acquisition of driver genes in breast cancer
Screening of chromosome arm-level aneuploidies uncovers that these alterations select for specific basal-like breast cancer driver genes, including PLGRKT, an oncogene whose tumour-promoting activity is associated with highly stress-resistant mitochondria and enhanced detoxification of reactive oxygen species.

Prior therapy defines mutation profiles in childhood cancer at relapse
Chemotherapy, particularly with platinum-based drugs, is associated with substantial, rapidly detectable mutagenesis in childhood cancers, tripling private signatures and doubling mutation burden, highlighting therapy-induced tumour evolution and opportunities for safer, de-escalated treatment.

Structural basis of the RNA-editing cascade in trypanosome mitochondria
Cryo-electron microscopy sheds light on the architecture of the Trypanosoma brucei mitochondrial editosome and reveals how this assembly mediates mRNA editing through the insertion and deletion of uridine nucleotides.
Yun-Tao Liu, Andres F. Vacas, Jonathan Jih et al.
TM184C is a GPCR-like regulator of intercellular exchange and autophagy
TM184C—an ancient G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-like superdark protein involved in regulation of autophagy, intercellular connectivity and material exchange—underscores the promise of exploring the understudied human proteome and beyond.
Kyutae D. Lee, Samuel Taylor, Jennifer Arcuri et al.
